newsitem.title: USA: U.S heating oil prices pare losses on ACCESS - Oct 10.
newsitem.headline: U.S heating oil prices pare losses on ACCESS - Oct 10.

text.p: U.S. heating oil prices pared their sharp losses in early ACCESS trade, with buying active and a possible recovery seen on Friday.
NYMEX November heating oil rose 0.18 of a cent a gallon early into ACCESS after-hours trade, trimming a 3.05-cent loss which saw prices settle at 70.92 cents. About 135 lots traded.
"I think people are buying back on the dips," one trader said. "It's definitely a correction indication. Whether it follows through on the floor (session), that's a different story," he added.

The slide in heating oil began when data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) and U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) showed a 1.3 million barrel rise in distillates stocks, which came out late Tuesday.
Traders said they doubted heating oil would fall to 70 cents a gallon on the correction.
After hours, NYMEX crude oil traded six cents higher at $24.32, after falling 81 cents early. The contract traded about 300 lots, with support seen on Friday at $24 a barrel and resistance at $25.
Gasoline edged to the upside after hours, with bids 63.52 cents a gallon and offers 64.30 cents, after settling 63.52 cents.
